title: 26 U.S.C. § 162, Trade or business expenses
publisher: Office of the Law Revision Counsel, U.S. House of Representatives
publication_date_or_edition: Preliminary 2026 U.S. Code text, page states law in force 2026-09-23
inspected_summary: Section 162(a) allows ordinary and necessary expenses paid or incurred in carrying on a trade or business; paragraph (a)(1) covers reasonable compensation for actual services.

evidence.method: Direct original-source page open and substantive section read
evidence.observed: The trade-or-business threshold and ordinary/necessary standard are distinct from who paid or booked the expense; compensation must be reasonable for actual services.

publisher: United States Tax Court opinion, public reproduction at OpenJurist
accounting_bases: US federal income tax, IRC §§162 and 212

title: 26 U.S.C. § 4941, Taxes on self-dealing
publisher: Office of the Law Revision Counsel, U.S. House of Representatives
inspected_summary: Section 4941 defines prohibited self-dealing transactions and includes a narrow exception for reasonable, nonexcessive compensation or reimbursement for personal services that are reasonable and necessary to carry out exempt purposes.
